root_cause.text: The function starfive_aes_aead_do_one_req() allocates memory for rctx->adata with kzalloc() but does not free it when error conditions (sg_copy_to_buffer() or starfive_aes_hw_init() failure) occur before the normal cleanup point, leading to a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds kfree(rctx->adata) in the error path for sg_copy_to_buffer() failure and kfree(rctx->adata) in the error path for starfive_aes_hw_init() failure (guarded by cryp->assoclen). The CVE description explicitly states that the allocated rctx->adata is freed unconditionally after write_adata operations, but not freed in these earlier error exits.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds kfree(rctx->adata) in the error path for sg_copy_to_buffer() failure and kfree(rctx->adata) in the error path for starfive_aes_hw_init() failure (guarded by cryp->assoclen). The CVE description explicitly states that the allocated rctx->adata is freed unconditionally after write_adata operations, but not freed in these earlier error exits.

candidates.rationale: Error return path after memory allocation failure; while not a leak itself, it is part of the error handling flow that could be related to the missing free.
Directly returns -EINVAL after sg_copy_to_buffer() failure without freeing rctx->adata, causing a memory leak.
Assigns the allocated rctx to ctx->rctx, marking the point where the allocated memory is stored and must be freed on error.
Calls starfive_aes_hw_init(), which can fail; if it fails, the subsequent return ret will leak rctx->adata.
Returns error code from starfive_aes_hw_init() without freeing rctx->adata, directly causing a memory leak.
Control flow statement that may bypass cleanup; if write_text does not free rctx->adata, this could lead to a leak under certain conditions.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is reached after sg_copy_to_buffer() fails but rctx->adata has already been allocated by kzalloc(). It returns an error code without freeing rctx->adata, directly causing a memory leak.

This statement returns the error code from starfive_aes_hw_init() without freeing rctx->adata. Since rctx->adata was allocated before the call, failure of starfive_aes_hw_init() results in a memory leak.

This assignment stores the pointer to the allocated request context (which includes the allocated rctx->adata) into ctx->rctx. Any error that occurs after this point (e.g., starfive_aes_hw_init failure) will bypass the normal cleanup that frees rctx->adata, making this statement part of the vulnerable path.

This function call can fail. When it returns an error, the subsequent 'return ret;' will leak rctx->adata because no free occurs before the return. The failure of starfive_aes_hw_init() is one of the two error conditions identified in the root cause that trigger the memory leak.

This unconditional jump to the write_text label occurs after a successful starfive_aes_hw_init(). If the write_text label and subsequent code do not properly free rctx->adata under certain conditions (e.g., if an error occurs later and cleanup is missed), this goto could contribute to a memory leak. It is included as a plausibly related control flow statement.

This statement is reached when kzalloc() for rctx->adata fails. While it does not directly cause a leak (allocation failed), it is part of the error handling flow and highlights the asymmetry: on other error paths (sg_copy_to_buffer, starfive_aes_hw_init) the allocated memory is not freed. Including it provides context for the vulnerable error handling pattern.
